description.narrative: Angola, Multicomponent, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP Angola)This program has the following goals: Reduce by 50% new infections from HIV/AIDS, among people of all ages, by 2026. Treat 75% of the persons diagnosed with HIV. Reduce the mother-to-child transmission rate from 15% in 2022 to 6% in 2026. Decrease TB incidence from 325 to 261 per 100.000 inhabitants by 2027 (325 per 100,000 is the incidence estimated by WHO in 2021). By 2025, reduce by 40% malaria morbidity in the country, in relation to the baseline of 2020 (positivity rate in 2020: 52%). By 2025, reduce by 50% malaria mortality in the country, in relation to the baseline of 2020 (mortality rate by 100,000 in 2020: 38). The objectives of this program are: By 2026, offer HIV combination prevention packages in at least 60% of the municipalities containing the highest HIV incidence rates among the priority population. By 2026, identify 75% of the persons estimated to be living with HIV and who do not know their status. By 2026, increase Viral Load Coverage among PLHIV to 75% and to 80% among pregnant women. Increase the case detection rate of TB by 5% per year (2024-2027). By 2027, increase the treatment success rate for TB-S from 68% to 78% among adults (5% increase per year during 4 years). By 2027, all the 82 municipalities with installed mWRD have medical doctors trained in MDR/RR-TB treatment. By 2027, promote one standard model of C-DOT in all municipalities. By 2025, provide malaria preventative services to at least 80% of the population at risk. By 2025, provide early diagnosis and treatment to 100% of malaria suspected cases. By 2025, strengthen the epidemiological and entomological surveillance systems, and monitoring and evaluation so that 100% of municipalities can achieve their malaria prevention and control targets. By the end of 2027, 90% of health facilities are reporting their monthly reports.. By the 2027, 90% of health facilities monthly reports are submitted timely.
